title: MCP tools expose an empty inputSchema (no properties), so clients/LLMs cannot discover arguments
evidence: main.cpp:74 toolList() builds every tool with inputSchema={"type":"object"} and no properties/required; args (season, competition, team, venue, ...) are named only in the description string. Demonstrated consequence in _factual.json: the standings probe could not pass a season and got an all-seasons 36-row/690-pt table.
suggestion: Add a JSON-Schema properties block per tool enumerating each argument (season, competition, team, team1/team2, name, nationality, club, venue, from/to, limit) so an MCP client/LLM can form narrow calls.

title: standings() merges every season when no season argument is given
evidence: main.cpp:71 the filter is (season.empty()||m.season==season||...) so with season absent it aggregates ALL seasons of the competition; _factual.json shows the resulting 36-row, 690-pt table. The capability itself is correct: passing season=2019 filters m.season=="2019" (data/kaggle/Brasileirao_Matches.csv col 8), which yields exactly 20 teams, and the self-test exercises standings with season=2023 (main.cpp:83,86).
suggestion: Default to the most recent season (or require season) when the argument is omitted, so the default call returns a single-season table rather than a lifetime aggregate.

title: Self-test uses only synthetic in-memory rows; never loads the real CSVs or drives the stdio loop
evidence: main.cpp:76-89 selftest() constructs a 3-match Database literal and asserts on it; it never calls Database::load(data/kaggle) nor feeds JSON-RPC through main(). test_coverage=1.0 (scores.json) reflects these synthetic scenarios passing, not real-data correctness.
suggestion: Add at least one scenario that loads data/kaggle and one that round-trips a tools/call request through the JSON-RPC loop, so regressions like the seasonless standings merge would be caught by tests.

title: Extremely dense one-liner style hurts idiomaticity/maintainability
evidence: main.cpp:66-73 each query function is a single ~500-char line; scores.json reports idiomatic=0.2 and maintainability=0.667.
suggestion: Break the query functions across multiple lines; the logic is sound but unreadable as written.
